question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $79u+35v=\text{gcd}(79,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}79 & = & 35\cdot 2 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 9\cdot 3 & + & 8 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 8\cdot 1 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(79,35)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =79-35\cdot 2 \\ 8 & =35-9\cdot 3 \\ 1 & =9-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =9-8 \\  & =9-[35-9\cdot 3] \\  & =9\cdot 4-35 \\  & =[79-35\cdot 2]\cdot 4-35 \\  & =79\cdot 4-35\cdot 9 \\  & =79\cdot 4+35\cdot (-9)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=4$ and $v=-9.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=4+(-9)=-5.
$$
